subject.title: Add maxThreads config for local embedding (node-llama-cpp)

question: Should OpenClaw expose `memorySearch.local.maxThreads` as a supported public config knob for the official local llama.cpp embedding provider?
rationale: The source gap and dependency support are clear, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config surfaces and this becomes a public tuning contract.

options.title: Approve narrow maxThreads config
options.body: Add only `memorySearch.local.maxThreads`, validate it as a non-negative integer or positive integer according to the chosen semantics, and forward it to `getLlama` without adding unrelated GPU or NUMA knobs.

options.title: Keep local threading implicit
options.body: Leave node-llama-cpp defaults in control and document existing alternatives such as Ollama or LM Studio if maintainers do not want another core memory config option.

options.title: Design broader local tuning separately
options.body: Treat CPU threads, GPU, NUMA, and related llama.cpp tuning as one explicit provider-plugin configuration design instead of merging this single knob now.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow maxThreads config
recommendation.body: Add only `memorySearch.local.maxThreads`, validate it as a non-negative integer or positive integer according to the chosen semantics, and forward it to `getLlama` without adding unrelated GPU or NUMA knobs.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about the memory-host/config boundary that recent history shows Peter has refactored and maintained.
